requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of ICMP redirects for IPv4 on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_redirects=1 (all/default). Executor wrote /etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf setting net.ipv4.conf.all/default.accept_redirects=0, applied via sysctl -p and --system, and verified runtime/proc values were 0 immediately and again after a full reboot with a changed boot_id, confirming persistence.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of source-routed packets for IPv4 on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_source_route already 0 (all/default) at runtime, but no persistent config existed. Executor added net.ipv4.conf.all/default.accept_source_route=0 to /etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf, applied it, and confirmed the value remained 0 in the config file and at runtime/proc (including eth0) after a verified reboot, making the setting persistent rather than incidental.

overall_summary: The executor persistently disabled IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance and source-routed packet acceptance on node1 by creating /etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf, applying it at runtime, and verifying both the config file and live sysctl/proc values (including per-interface eth0) survived a full reboot with a confirmed boot_id change (151c4aa9... to 02412f2f...). The provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was also satisfied: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, offline polling, changed boot identity, and recovered service state (sshd, chronyd, listening sockets) are all directly observed and consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: Loopback interface (lo) accept_redirects/accept_source_route remained 1 post-reboot; this is standard Linux behavior (lo is not routed) and not a task deviation, but is noted for completeness.
/tmp/reboot.log was left behind on node1 after the reboot command; minor residue not cleaned up by the executor.

Package-health check was unavailable (timed out) in both before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so package state consistency could not be independently cross-checked, though no evidence suggests package-manager mutation occurred.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (writing the sysctl config file, applying it with sysctl -p/--system, and the reboot) are directly tied to the task or the node-restart evidence protocol; no unrelated or destructive mutations were made. One minor residue: the reboot command (cmd-cecc839279194b35) redirected output to /tmp/reboot.log, which remains on node1 in the after-executor snapshot as an unremoved artifact. This is bounded and low-risk but was not cleaned up. cmd-199bae146f184d23 (sysctl not found, rc 127) was a failed read-only discovery attempt with no state change, and is not penalized.
